title: The Journey to the Tin Woodman
chineseTitle: 第一章 前往铜人王国的旅程

paragraphs.en: Tip, drenched and dripping, ordered the Saw-Horse to stay still. The horse complied, floating calmly on the water.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人正浑身湿透、滴答作响，命令木马呆在原地。木马遵命而行，在水面上静静地漂浮着。

paragraphs.en: "Why did you call me a fool?" asked the horse.
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么说我傻瓜？”马儿问道。

paragraphs.en: "It's just when I'm angry," admitted Tip.
paragraphs.zh: “这只是在我生气的时候，”蒂普承认道。

paragraphs.en: "Then I'll call you one too," replied the horse. "I didn't make this river; only a term of reproach fits for being upset with me."
paragraphs.zh: “那我也会叫你一声。”马儿回答道，“这河不是我造成的，用不着因此责备我。”

paragraphs.en: Tip acknowledged his mistake and instructed the Saw-Horse to paddle towards the shore. Slowly, they reached dry land.
paragraphs.zh: 提普承认了自己的错误，并指示木马锯子朝岸边划去。渐渐地，他们抵达了干燥的陆地。

paragraphs.en: Tip freed himself and his companions from the cords. He heard the Scarecrow fall with a mushy sound. Checking on Jack, he found the wooden body still atop the horse, but the pumpkin head was missing.
paragraphs.zh: 提普挣脱了绳索，解救了同伴们。他听到稻草人发出一种软绵绵的声音摔了下来。检查杰克的情况时，他发现木马的身躯仍矗立在马上，但南瓜脑袋却不见了踪影。

paragraphs.en: The straw had packed into the lower part of the Scarecrow's body, making it plump, while the upper half looked empty. The heavy crown, sewn to prevent loss, now hung limply, crushing the painted face into a pug dog-like shape.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草填充了麦田守望者身体的下半部分，使其显得圆鼓鼓的，而上半身则空荡荡的。原本沉重的王冠被缝制以防丢失，现在松垮地垂挂着，压得画出的脸庞扁平如斗牛犬。

paragraphs.en: Tip hurried towards the river, worried about his friend Man Jack. The Scarecrow was intact, but the pumpkin head essential for Jack's survival was missing. Spotting a long pole nearby, Tip cautiously approached the water where he saw the golden pumpkin bobbing gently.
paragraphs.zh: 提普急忙向河边跑去，心里挂念着朋友曼·杰克。稻草人完好无损，但对杰克生存至关重要的南瓜头却不见了。他注意到附近有一根长杆，便小心翼翼地靠近水面，只见一个金色的南瓜在水中轻轻起伏。

paragraphs.en: The pumpkin was initially out of reach, but eventually floated closer. With the pole, Tip retrieved it and brought it to shore. He carefully wiped the wet face with his handkerchief before placing it back on Jack's neck.
paragraphs.zh: 南瓜最初够不着，但最终漂得更近了。用棍子一撑，蒂普把它捞了起来，并带回了岸边。他小心地用手帕擦干南瓜的脸，然后才把它放回杰克的脖子上。

paragraphs.en: "Dear me!" Jack exclaimed. "What a dreadful experience!
paragraphs.zh: “天哪！”杰克脱口而出，“真是可怕的经历啊！

paragraphs.en: I wonder if water can spoil pumpkins?"
paragraphs.zh: 我倒是要问问，水会不会让南瓜变坏？

paragraphs.en: Tip focused on helping the Scarecrow instead. He removed the wet straw from the King’s body and legs, spreading it to dry in the sun. Meanwhile, he hung Jack’s damp clothes over the Saw-Horse.
paragraphs.zh: 蒂普则一心一意地帮助稻草人。他把国王身上的湿稻草和腿上的湿稻草取下，摊开在阳光下晾干。与此同时，他还把杰克的湿衣服挂在木马身上晾晒。

paragraphs.en: Jack sighed deeply. “If water spoils pumpkins,” he mused, “then my days are numbered.”
paragraphs.zh: 杰克深深叹了口气。“如果水能腐烂南瓜，”他沉思道，“那么我的日子也不多了。”

paragraphs.en: Tip replied, “I’ve never noticed that; unless the water is boiling. If your head isn’t cracked, you’re in good shape.”
paragraphs.zh: Tip 回答说：“我可没注意到这一点，除非水是沸水。如果你的脑袋没有出问题，那你状况不错。”

paragraphs.en: “Indeed, it’s not cracked at all,” Jack said more cheerfully.
paragraphs.zh: “事实上，并没有裂开。”杰克高兴地说。

paragraphs.en: “Then don’t worry,” Tip retorted. “Care once killed a cat.”
paragraphs.zh: “那你大可放心吧，”蒂普反驳道，“关心曾经害死过一只猫。”

paragraphs.en: Jack added seriously, “So I am very glad I’m not a cat.”
paragraphs.zh: 杰克认真地说：“所以我非常高兴我不是一只猫。”

paragraphs.en: The sun dried their clothes quickly. Tip stirred the straw to absorb moisture and reshape the Scarecrow. Once done, he smoothed out the face, restoring its usual charming expression.
paragraphs.zh: 太阳很快就把他们的衣服晒干了。蒂普搅拌着稻草，吸收其中的湿气并重新塑形稻草人。完成后，他轻轻抚平稻草人的脸庞，恢复了它那往常迷人的表情。

paragraphs.en: “Thank you,” the monarch said brightly, finding himself well balanced. “Being a Scarecrow has its advantages; with friends nearby, nothing serious can happen.”
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢，”国王脸上带着明媚的笑容，发现自己站得稳当。“作为稻草人也有它的好处；有朋友在身边，什么严重的事也不会发生。”

paragraphs.en: Jack then wondered aloud, “I wonder if hot sunshine could crack pumpkins.”
paragraphs.zh: 杰克不禁脱口而出：“不知烈日是否能把南瓜晒裂？”

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow reassured Tip that he had nothing to fear except old age. They remounted the Saw-Horse, with Tip holding onto the post, Jack clinging to Tip, and the Pumpkinhead wrapped in the Scarecrow's arms.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人宽慰蒂普，告诉他除了年老外没有什么好怕的。他们重新骑上了木马，蒂普抓着木桩，杰克依附在蒂普身上，南瓜头则被稻草人紧紧抱在怀里。

paragraphs.en: "Go slowly," advised Tip to his horse, "no danger of pursuit now."
paragraphs.zh: “慢慢走吧，”提普对他的马建议道，“现在不用担心追击的危险了。”

paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse responded gruffly, while the Pumpkinhead asked if he was hoarse. The horse growled at being insulted but Tip soothed him, reminding them they must remain friends.
paragraphs.zh: 铁马粗声粗气地回应，而南瓜头则问它是不是嗓子哑了。马儿被侮辱后 growled 出声，但提普安慰了他，提醒他们必须保持朋友关系。

paragraphs.en: The Saw-Horse declared he had no use for the Pumpkinhead, who lost his head too easily. They rode in silence until the Scarecrow recalled saving Dorothy from bees on this very spot. He explained that Nick Chopper, their friend the Tin Woodman, destroyed the Grey Wolves there and how Winged Monkeys captured them with Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: 铁马声明自己对南瓜头没有好感，认为他太容易失去理智。他们默默骑行了一段时间，直到稻草人想起了在此地救过多萝西免遭蜜蜂攻击的事情。他解释说，他们的朋友锡木人尼克·切弗曾经在那里消灭了灰狼，并且讲述了翡翠城的飞猴是如何俘虏了他们和多萝西的。

paragraphs.en: Jack asked if Winged Monkeys ate pumpkins, but the Scarecrow said they were now Glinda's slaves, bound by her Golden Cap. The Scarecrow lost himself in thoughts of past adventures as they continued their journey under the setting sun.
paragraphs.zh: 杰克问 whether 飞猴是否吃南瓜，但稻草人说他们现在是oglala 的奴隶，被她的金帽所束缚。稻草人一边继续在落日下前行，一边沉浸在过去的冒险回忆中。

paragraphs.en: Night fell, and Tip stopped the horse for them to dismount.
paragraphs.zh: 夜幕降临，蒂普停下了马匹，让他们下来休息。

paragraphs.en: The boy yawned tiredly and suggested they lie down to sleep. Jack disagreed, stating he couldn't sleep either. The Saw-Horse declared he didn't know what sleep was.
paragraphs.zh: 男孩打着哈欠，提议躺下来睡觉。杰克不同意，说他也没法入睡。木马宣称自己根本不知道什么是睡眠。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow, thoughtful as always, proposed they consider the boy's fatigue. He recalled Dorothy often slept through the night during their journey. Tip admitted he was both tired and hungry.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人像往常一样沉思着，提议他们考虑那个男孩的疲劳问题。他回忆起，在他们的旅途中，多萝西经常整晚都在睡觉。蒂普承认自己又累又饿。

paragraphs.en: Jack gloomily noted a new danger: the boy might eat pumpkins. The boy laughed, saying he only liked stewed pumpkin pies. Jack angrily accused the Saw-Horse of being a coward.
paragraphs.zh: 杰克忧郁地注意到一个新的危险：那男孩可能会吃南瓜。男孩笑着解释说他只喜欢炖南瓜派。杰克生气地指责木马锯驹胆小如鼠，是个懦夫。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow interrupted, urging them not to quarrel. They all had weaknesses and should be considerate. Since Tip was hungry but had nothing to eat, they agreed to stay quiet so he could sleep.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人打断他们，劝大家不要争吵。每个人都有自己的弱点，应该互相体谅。既然蒂普饿得厉害又没什么吃的，大家决定暂时保持沉默，让他能够安心睡觉。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow added that in sleep, even hunger can be forgotten.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人补充说，在睡眠中，甚至饥饿都可以忘却。

paragraphs.en: Tip gratefully thanked the Scarecrow for his wisdom. He stretched out on the grass, using the Scarecrow's form as a pillow and soon fell asleep.
paragraphs.zh: Tip 感激地向稻草人道谢，感谢他提供的智慧。他躺在草地上，用稻草人的形状当枕头，很快就进入了梦乡。
